chunks: And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

“Badr took place in the month of Ramaḍān, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not perform iʿtikāf. Then, when the following year came, he performed iʿtikāf for twenty days: ten for that year, and ten as a make-up for what had passed him by.”

key_terms.بَدْرٌ: the Battle of Badr, the well-known early Islamic battle
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the sacred month of fasting
key_terms.قَضَاءً: as make-up for a missed act
key_terms.يَعْتَكِفْ: to perform iʿtikāf, spiritual retreat in the mosque

ai.seo_question: Why did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله perform twenty days of iʿtikāf after the Battle of Badr?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was unable to perform iʿtikāf during Ramaḍān in the year of Badr. In the following year, he performed twenty days of iʿtikāf, combining the current year's observance with a make-up for what he had missed, indicating the continuity and importance of this act of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "The Battle of Badr occurred in the Month of Ramadan, so the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) did not perform i'tikaf that year. However, in the following year, he performed i'tikaf for twenty days: ten days for that year's obligation and ten days as compensation for what he had missed."
